propositions: prev_snapshot.json grows to 228.1 MB (4.5 MB per day) because it stores full ACLI payloads; narrowing it to a bare key-set dict {jira_key: {}} reduces HEAD to 19,960 bytes vs 27.1 MB
218 of 399 consecutive snapshot pairs have identical key-sets, producing no commit; mean symmetric difference when keys change is 1.78 keys, validating that key-set storage is safe

The production call-site filter drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions empirically guards against unexpected mutations reaching Jira; corpus mutation-diff over 4 real pairs with full vs key-set prev showed zero observable differences

Key-set storage eliminates wasted raw (outbound, create, unbound_local) mutations (973–998 per pass) that arise when the fetch window shrinks or project is re-targeted, reducing differ work without changing Jira-facing behavior

Prev-shape-sensitive consumers check_dual_identity_complete and the differ's local-only/emit-both arms require mapping entries via local_state[key] or {} guards; storing dict {jira_key: {}} satisfies these constraints while full-payload and key-set shapes remain coexistent on first cutover pass
